column1: # Côte d'Ivoire (`ci.default`, class D (none): Calculated by Taqwa; the Africa region's conventions with COSIM's printed
# floors, Generic.kt's coteDIvoireRegion and coteDIvoireAt), gated first by the safe defaults lane (12 Nov 2026) and
# held to the trust audit's F3, F5 and F21 on 13 Nov 2026. REAL rows: Côte d'Ivoire's 183 app cities were routed to
# default.safe.africa, and the only tables held for the country are COSIM's (the Supreme Council of Imams, Mosques and
# Islamic Affairs, the national council of imams, which sets Ramadan and Eid with CODISS and labels its Dhuhr and Asr
# "Heure conventionnelle en Côte d'Ivoire"; the engine survey of 11 Nov 2026).
# What is held, and what kind of proof each row is (the audit's F21: said plainly):
# - FOUR REAL TABLES, all of them Abidjan's, at the app's own Abidjan point (archive/raw/manual/ci-cosim/2026-11-11/
#   - the month calendar of Joumada al-Oula 1448 (12 Oct to 10 Nov 2026), an image transcribed by hand: Soubh (also the
#     end of eating out of Ramadan: no imsak is printed then, the stricter reading), sunrise, the conventional Zouhr
#   - the Ramadan editions of 1434 (9 Jul to 8 Aug 2013) and 1436 (18 Jun to 18 Jul 2015): Imsak (the end of eating),
#   - the month calendar of Joumada al-Thaniya 1448 (10 Nov to 8 Dec 2026), fetched on 13 Nov 2026 after ci.default's
#     floors were set: the one HELD-OUT table of this file. Its 29 days are 28 held-out place-days: 10 Nov is printed in
#     both months, and a day a fit row also holds is not counted as held out (the block still shows 29 checks a time).
#     No cell is left out. READINGS, not the print, named in the table's own header (the lane's reviews, 14 Nov 2026):
#     its Maghreb and Icha column prints thirty rows beside twenty-nine dated days, so each day is held to the LATER of
#     the two rows that may be its own (Maghreb a minute later than the first reading on six days and Icha on eight; no
#     day earlier), and three misprinted cells are read by their column (the sunrise of 5 Dec, printed with a stray
#     third digit in its minutes, read without it; the sunrise of 6 Dec, printed ten minutes earlier than its column runs,
#     read ten minutes later; the second Icha row, printed an hour after its column, read an hour earlier) and
#     bind as a printed cell would.
#     What "held out" is true of: no START margin of ci.default was read off this table, and every start cleared it
#     untouched. It is NOT true of the end of eating any more: the rule rows below found the end a minute after
#     Soubh - 25 on three days of the 1448 months, days this table prints among them, the end-of-eating margin was then
#     set to the region's 2 min, and the end-of-eating late limit was read again with this table in it.
#   The first three are fit rows: ci.default's floors (the conventional Zouhr and Asr, the 25-minute end of eating) were
# - 136 ROWS DERIVED BY RULE, NOT PRINTED BY COSIM (68 places × the two 1448 months; the lane's first review, 14 Nov
#   2026), every one a fit row and an ends-only row (column E alone: it adds no place-day). The 1448 months print no
#   imsak, so nothing checked the end of eating out of Ramadan against COSIM's own rule on the newest Soubh held. Each
#   of these tables is the imsak rule of the Ramadan 1436 edition (Soubh - 25 on every day) on a month's printed Soubh,
#   at Abidjan and, moved by the printed minutes, at each of the 67 towns. They prove that the end of eating never
#   comes after the rule on the 1448 Soubh; they are not a time COSIM printed.
# - 268 DERIVED ROWS OF 67 TOWNS (67 × the four tables), every one a fit row. Both Ramadan editions print COSIM's
#   "CORRESPONDANCES HORAIRES": its times hold as printed for Abidjan, Adzopé, Afféry, Agboville, Anyama, Bingerville,
#   Bongouanou, Daoukro and Prikro, and every other town it lists takes them a whole number of minutes earlier or
#   later, the same in both editions (Bondoukou − 6 to Danané + 18). A derived table is Abidjan's + the printed minutes,
#   as COSIM defines them: the two Ramadan editions on every time, and the 1448 months on Soubh, sunrise, Maghreb and
#   Icha, their Zouhr and Asr kept at the conventional 13:00 and 16:00 printed for the whole country. The months print
#   no correspondences, so their derived rows carry the Ramadan editions' construction to them.
#   A derived row is NOT a table COSIM printed for the town, and it is not held-out evidence: the engine holds the same
#   minutes (Generic.cosimTowns) and reproduces the row by construction. What it proves is narrower: that the
#   implementation holds COSIM's printed rule for the town, and that the town's own sun never puts a start before the
#   rule or an end after it. So of the 68 places below, one (Abidjan) is proven against COSIM's own print and 67 against
#   COSIM's rule; the stamp's heldOut block counts Abidjan's 28 days alone.
#   46 of the 67 towns are app cities, at the app's own point. The other 21 the app does not list (the audit's F3 and
#   F5: Prikro, Alépé, Nassian, Sinématiali, Tiéningboué, Kani, Morondo, Dioulatiédougou, Djibrosso, Guintéguéla,
#   Madinani, Goulia, Tiémé, Bako, Booko, Tienko, Seydougou, Koonan, Toulépleu, Bin-Houyé, Koro): each at the town's
#   point as the lane knows it, approximate, which Generic.kt says with a 30 km band (60 for the villages).
# - WHAT IS NOT HELD: any day from 9 Dec to 17 Jun, the season of Ramadan 1448 (February and March 2027) included, or
#   from 9 Aug to 11 Oct; any town's own printed table; correspondences for a month calendar. The first table nobody
#   has seen is the calendar of Rajab 1448 (from about 9 Dec 2026), then COSIM's Ramadan 1448 edition.
# Found on the Africa region (the safe defaults lane): Dhuhr 49 to 50 min and Asr 37 min before COSIM's conventional
# times on every day of the month, and its end of eating after the 1436 imsak (Soubh − 25) on every day of that
# Found on ci.default with Abidjan's floors and every time at the town's own sun (the lane's review, 12 Nov 2026): Fajr
# before the derived Soubh on 1,297 of 4,232 place-days, at 24 towns, every day of both Ramadan editions in the north
# and the west (up to 8 min at Tengréla, 7 at Korhogo, Ferké, Odienné and Borotou-Koro, 5 at Bouna; none in the
# October-November month), and the end of eating a minute after the derived imsak at Adiaké (15 days) and Tabou (8).
# COSIM moves a town by whole minutes, not by its sun: in the northern summer the town's own dawn comes well before
# Abidjan's moved by its figure. The fix (Generic.coteDIvoireAt): beside the user's own point, a start point and an end
# point at Abidjan's latitude moved by the nearest printed town's minutes (as BIK's town figures, xk-bik.tsv), so every
# start is never before the region's own at Abidjan plus them and every end never after.
# Found on that with the 21 unlisted towns' rows added (the trust audit, 13 Nov 2026): Fajr 1 min before the derived
# Soubh at Madinani on 50 place-days (25 days of each Ramadan edition): the town was not in the engine's list, so a
# place there took the nearest listed town's lower figure. The fix (ruling R208): every town COSIM prints is held,
# listed by the app or not; a town held at an approximate point may be the nearest anywhere within its band, and a
# place takes the latest minutes of the towns that may be its nearest for its starts and the earliest for its ends.
# After it: 0 early, 0 late ends over the 272 rows then held. What it cost: in 2027, over the app's 183 cities, Fajr later on
# 3,786 place-days, Asr on 1,118, Maghrib on 3,561 and Isha on 3,324, by up to 6 min (Dianra), sunrise earlier on 1,989
# (up to 7, Dabakala) and the end of eating on 1,900 (up to 6); no start earlier, no end later, Dhuhr unchanged.
# No margin moved for a derived row.
# Found on that with the 136 rule rows added (the lane's first review, 14 Nov 2026): the end of eating 1 min after the
# rule on three days of November and December 2026. The lane had measured "0 to 1 min before the imsak, at least 40 s on every
# day" on the 1436 edition and carried it to every month; on the 1448 Soubh it does not hold (the fitter asks for
# 38 s). The fix: endOfEatingMarginSeconds = -120, the margin every region takes, in place of none. After it: 0 early,
# 0 late ends over all 408 rows; against the rule the end is at least 1 min before it everywhere, up to 3 at Abidjan and up to 7 at Seydougou.
# What it cost: the end of eating 2 min earlier on every day, everywhere in the country; no start moved.
# COSIM's own construction puts its Maghreb before the town's own sunset in the north in summer (up to 9 min at Tengréla,
# 8 at Kolia, 6 to 7 at Bouna, Ferké, Bondoukou and Korhogo, in the 1436 edition's June and July days); the app's Maghrib
# never comes before the sun's own, so there it runs up to 16 min after COSIM's.
# The end of eating (the audit's F36): COSIM prints an imsak in Ramadan only (Soubh − 25 in 1436, − 15 in 1434); the
# app ends eating 27 min before its 15° dawn (the rule's 25 and the 2 min margin) on every day of the year, the safe
# side, so out of Ramadan it runs up to 28 min before COSIM's Soubh at Abidjan and up to 32 at Seydougou, and at least
# 30 min before the Fajr the app itself shows (which is 3 min after that dawn, rounded up). In Ramadan it is up to 13 min
# before the 1434 edition's imsak at Abidjan (24 at its towns). Kept, said in the app's method sentence, and put to
# Dhuhr's end (the audit's F2): the fixed 16:00 holds Asr's start only; Dhuhr ends at the Standard Asr the sky gives,
# up to 45 min before it. No table prints an end of Dhuhr, so no row checks it: DayComputerTest holds the rule.
